title: Study evaluating two treatment strategies for rectal cancer in patients ≥75 years old
official: NACRE 2_Randomized phase III study evaluating two treatment strategies for locally advanced rectal cancer in patients ≥75 years old
summary: Main objective: To compare efficacy of SCRT followed by 6 cycles of FOLFOX4s chemotherapy versus SCRT without chemotherapy in terms of organ preservation rate in elderly patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (cT3-T4).
conditions:
Patients ≥75 years old with cT3/T4 rectal adenocarcinoma eligible to radiotherapy,
FOLFOX chemotherapy and total mesorectal excision (TME) surgery
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Histologically confirmed diagnosis of adenocarcinoma of the rectum
2. Patients must be affiliated to a Social Security System (or equivalent).
3. Patient must have signed a written informed consent prior to any trial specific procedures. When the patient is physically unable to give their written consent, a trusted person of their choice, independent from the investigator or the sponsor, can confirm in writing the patient’s consent
4. Patients must be willing and able to comply with the protocol for the duration of the study including scheduled visits, treatment plan, laboratory tests and other study procedures
5. Age ≥75 years
6. WHO performance status 0-1
7. cT3a-b with maximum diameter > 5 cm, T3c-d or cT4 tumor on pretreatment pelvic MRI
8. General condition considered suitable for radical pelvic surgery and a systemic therapy with FOLFOX,
9. Distal part of the tumor ≤10 cm from the anal margin, the measurement done by pelvic MRI
10. Oncogeriatrician approval
11. Adequate biological function defined by: a. Neutrophils ≥ 1500/mm3 b. Platelets ≥ 100 000/mm3 c. Hemoglobin ≥ 10g/dL d. Total bilirubin ≤ 1,5 x ULN e. Alkaline phosphatases ≤ 1,5 x ULN f. Creatinine clearance >50mL/mn (MDRD) g.Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels 2.5× ULN
12. Men must agree to use adequate contraception methods during treatment and at least until 12 months after the end of the treatment with oxaliplatin
Exclusion criteria:
1. Metastatic disease
2. Non resectable cancer, including extension to prostate or extension to perineal muscles
3. History of pelvic irradiation
4. Contraindication to FOLFOX 4s chemotherapy:  Regarding the treatment with 5-fluorouracil: ➢ Recent (within the last 4 weeks) or concomitant treatment with brivudine ➢ Presence of a potentially serious infection Receipt of a live or live-attenuated vaccine within 30 days prior to the first dose of the study intervention ➢ Poor nutritional status/Clinically significant active heart disease or myocardial infarction within the past 6 months, given the cardiotoxicity of fluorouracil. Regarding the treatment with oxaliplatin: Due to the cardiotoxicity of oxaliplatin (risk of QT prolongation as described in section 4.4 of the oxaliplatin SmPC): ➢ hypokalemia less than normal ➢ hypomagnesemia ➢ hypocalcemia ➢ QT/QTc interval longer than 450 msec for men and longer than 470 msec for women on the inclusion ECG; Peripheral sensory neuropathy with functional impairment prior to the first treatment, according to the oxaliplatin SmPC. Known history of hypersensitivity to fluorouracil, oxaliplatin, folinic acid, or any of their excipients, as stated in the respective SmPCs.
5. Contraindication to MRI
6. Microsatellite instability (MSI) and/or mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR)
7. Complete or partial Dihydropyrimidine Deshydrogenase (DPD) deficiency (uracilemia ≥ 16 ng/mL)
8. Arterial or venous thrombotic or embolic events such as cerebrovascular accident (including transient ischemic attacks), deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism within 6 months before start of treatment
9. Contradiction radiotherapy and/or TME surgery
10. Any other serious concomitant disease or disorder that may interfere with the patient's participation in the study and safety during the study (e.g., severe liver, heart, kidney, lung, metabolic, or psychiatric disorders).
11. Concurrent treatment with other experimental drugs or other anti-cancer therapy, treatment in a clinical trial within 30 days prior to randomization
12. Any psychiatric disorder precluding understanding of information of trial related topics and giving informed consent
13. No prior chemotherapy or surgery for rectal cancer
14. Any serious underlying medical condition (as judged by the investigator) that could impair the ability of the patient to participate in the trial
15. Persons deprived of their liberty or under protective custody or guardianship.
16. Patients unwilling or unable to comply with the medical follow-up required by the trial because of geographic, familial, social, or psychological reasons.
17. Other cancer within 3 years prior to rectal cancer diagnosis (except for in situ cancer and basal cell carcinoma of the skin)
